question: What changes when the same independently seeded roots execute sequentially or in processes?
scope: Execution control with identical forests. No episodes or playing strength evaluation. This protocol follows the earlier scaling study and does not alter its results.
root_adjustment: Create each ordinary scenario from random.Random(300), then set player.pips to 7. Preserve every other state field. Check the serialized root before and after each execution.
allocation: All phases call the same fixed work path. Configured workers count independent roots, even in sequential execution. Each total is split by quotient and remainder. Seeds derive from mcts-root-v1 and stable worker IDs. Roots are evaluated in worker ID order sequentially and merged in that same order in every phase.
order: Run the six listed conditions in order and each phase in its listed order. The six permutations put each phase twice in each ordinal position. There is one observation per scenario, root count and phase. Do not select the order from measured results.
timing: Sequential and cold wall time include engine construction and the search call. Warm prepares a fresh engine and process pool before starting its search timer. Pool preparation and startup are retained separately. No unrecorded search is used to warm the pool. This initialized pool differs from the second search warm phase in the earlier study. All phases build fresh trees. Pool cleanup is outside the search timer.
identity: Require exact equality of assigned work, worker IDs and seeds, complete and known work, unused allowances, virtual visits, stopping reasons, errors, every raw visit and value sum, ranked actions and their means. Only report and worker elapsed times and pool startup time are excluded. Match process phases against sequential execution. Keep unequal receipts and paths in the record if a comparison fails.
metrics: warm preparation and pool startup seconds
same forest computational equality and any differing paths
actual and unused simulations and transitions
ranked actions, raw root statistics and stopping reasons
analysis: Retain individual times and sequential wall time divided by cold or warm wall time only for a complete identical forest. These six fixed conditions do not establish general scaling, speedup, stronger play or significance. Wall time differences include interpreter, scheduling, construction and process orchestration effects. They are not pure IPC latency. No new parameter tuning follows the outcomes.
resource_policy: At most four owned process workers. Stop competing agent tests, renderers and measurements during collection. Preserve ordinary applications and settings. Record observed shared machine conditions without claiming exclusive machine access.
failure_policy: Write a running cell before starting it and save each result before another execution. Preserve the first attempt and partial worker accounting. Stop on an execution failure, root mutation, interrupted call or computational mismatch. Do not retry failed work or replace unfavorable timings. A corrected implementation needs a new committed revision and separate output. The sequential path has no process watchdog, and caller interrupts remain visible.
source_identity: Require a clean committed tree. Record full revision and normalized hashes of this protocol, runner, imported report and checkpoint helpers, engine, game and source data. Verify those sources again after collection. Commit and review implementation and protocol before executing the study.
reproduction: python tools/run_same_forest.py --output same-forest-study.json --conditions "Describe the observed measurement conditions"
